title: Depth Zero Theta Lift via Finite Fields
body_html:
Depth Zero Theta Lift via Finite Fields

For a good lattice \(L\) representing a vertex \(x\), the finite reductive quotient of \(G_x\) decomposes into unitary groups attached to the residue spaces \[ \ell=L/L^\ast p_D,\qquad \ell^\ast=L^\ast/L. \] Thus a depth zero representation decomposes as \(\rho_\ell\otimes\rho_{\ell^\ast}\).

For two vertices \(x\) and \(x'\), the depth zero \(K\)-type \((x',\rho')\) is a theta lift of \((x,\rho)\) if the finite-field representations satisfy the two finite oscillator correspondences \[ \rho_{\ell'^\ast}\in \theta_{\ell,\ell'^\ast}(\rho_\ell), \qquad \rho_{\ell'}\in \theta_{\ell^\ast,\ell'}(\rho_{\ell^\ast}). \] For cuspidal \(\rho\), the relevant finite-field theta lift is unique at first occurrence.

For a depth zero supercuspidal datum \(\Sigma=(x,0,1,\rho)\), the data-level lift \(\#_{V,T'}(\Sigma)\) is obtained by taking these first-occurrence finite-field lifts in the target Witt tower and rebuilding the target depth-zero datum.
